newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran denies inviting Taleban's envoy for talks.
newsitem.headline: Iran denies inviting Taleban's envoy for talks.

text.p: Iran on Saturday denied inviting the foreign minister of Afghanistan's Taleban militia to visit Tehran, but said it was ready to host talks among fighting Afghan factions.
"We have made no invitation to Taleban," Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati was quoted as saying by Tehran radio.
"If Afghan groups and the Afghan government are to hold talks...We are ready to host inter-Afghan negotiations in the near future in Iran," Velayati said.
Iran, which has often criticised the Sunni Moslem Taleban, has continued to recognise the government of ousted President Burhanuddin Rabbani.

Taleban's deputy foreign minister, Mullah Abdul Jalil, told Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) last week that Iran had invited the Islamic movement's foreign minister, Mullah Mohammad Ghaus, to Tehran to try to improve strained relations.
AIP said Ghaus would urge Iran to stop what he called its assistance to Taleban's foes. Iran denies helping any Afghan faction.
Tehran has repeatedly called on Afghan factions to stop fighting and reach a power-sharing agreement.

The Taleban are fighting forces loyal to Rabbani's military commander Ahmad Shah Masood and those of General Abdul Rashid Dostum on frontlines about 40 km (25 miles) north of Kabul and in remote northwestern provinces of Afghanistan.
